error.window:range: The date ranges are incorrect. The last date of each range must be after the first date, and the last arrival date must be after the first departure date.

mission.replaceQuestion: This operation closes the mission "{name}". Save the mission first to keep your changes.

orbit.label: Top view of the plan. Time of flight: {days} d.
orbit.caption: View from the north pole of the ecliptic. The +X axis points to the equinox of J2000. Each label shows the number of the encounter, the body and the date ({scale}). A diamond shows a deep-space maneuver.

plan.entryAltitude: Periapsis altitude of the approach orbit
plan.apoapsisHint: From the center of the body.
plan.bAngle: Angle of the aim point in the B-plane
plan.bAngleHint: The angle is from the T axis in the direction of the R axis.
plan.coastDays: Flight time after the last flyby
plan.coastHint: 0: the application sets the time from the size of the sphere of influence.
plan.notOk: The plan has no solution for one or more legs. Change the dates or the options of the leg.
plan.rla: Right ascension of the launch asymptote (ICRF)
plan.dvDep: Departure burn from the parking orbit ({alt} km)
plan.propellant: Propellant for the Δv after the launch
plan.noPropellant: The plan uses {need} kg of propellant. The spacecraft has {have} kg.
plan.legNote: a: semi-major axis. e: eccentricity. i: inclination to the reference plane of the frame ({frame}). rp, ra: periapsis radius and apoapsis radius. Rev.: complete revolutions.

transfer.title: Transfer
transfer.intro: This screen calculates the orbit from one body to a second body for the dates that you give. The model is two-body motion about the Sun (Lambert problem).
transfer.findBestNote: The search starts at the departure date. It finds the dates with the minimum total Δv in one synodic period.
transfer.retrograde: Retrograde transfer (opposite to the motion of the planets)
transfer.optionsNote: With one or more complete revolutions, the transfer has two solutions for the same dates.
transfer.periapsisSun: Periapsis radius of the transfer orbit
transfer.makeMission: Make a mission from these dates
transfer.hohmannNote: The reference is a Hohmann transfer between two circular orbits in one plane. The radii are the semi-major axes of the two bodies: {r1} au and {r2} au. The actual orbits are not circular and are not in one plane, thus the values are different.
transfer.modelNote: The values on this screen come from the patched-conic model. To get values from the full force model, make a mission and calculate the flight.

windows.title: Launch windows
windows.intro: The map shows the launch energy and the velocity changes for each pair of a departure date and an arrival date. Bright areas show transfers that use less energy.
windows.autoNote: The ranges then include one synodic period after the first departure date.
windows.both: Also calculate retrograde transfers and use the better one
windows.examplesNote: Each button makes the map for the first leg of an actual mission. The map then shows the actual launch date and the actual encounter date.
windows.mapLabel: Map of {quantity} for transfers from {from} to {to}. Horizontal axis: departure date. Vertical axis: arrival date.
windows.mapNote: Click the map to select a pair of dates. The contour lines have the values of the color scale. Each transfer has less than one revolution.
windows.best: Dates with the minimum total Δv
windows.noTransfer: There is no transfer for these dates: the arrival is before the departure.
windows.exampleCheck: Test of the actual launch: this application gives C3 = {ours} km²/s². The JPL Horizons trajectory gives {actual} km²/s². The difference is {diff} %.
windows.toTransfer: Open these dates in the Transfer screen
windows.empty: There is no map. Calculate the map.
